plan.summary: Two primary-source upgrades found while auditing the final Oct 21 Gemini batch (both re-checked here): Ain't No Mo's amended SEC Form D/A states the offering was capitalized at $5,696,583 (replacing the NYT up-to $5.5M from plan bro-5647-k), and Tootsie's weekly figure becomes Broadway Journal's $858,000 break-even from offering documents (was an unsourced $800,000; Gemini had wrongly given this figure to Hillary and Clinton). Old values from the private core data at 73898e0.

actions.description: aint-no-mo-2022: the amended Form D gives the amount raised

actions.oldValue: New York Times (Dec 9, 2022), on its early closing: "The show was capitalized for up to $5.5 million," based on an SEC filing. https://www.nytimes.com/2022/12/09/theater/aint-no-mo-broadway-closing.html
actions.newValue: SEC Form D/A filing (Ain't No Mo Broadway LLC, CIK 0001914790, filed Jan 24, 2023): "New maximum capitalization was $6,000,000/new minimum capitalization was $5,000,000 - offering capitalized at $5,696,583." The New York Times (Dec 9, 2022) had reported "capitalized for up to $5.5 million" from the earlier filing. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1914790/000191479023000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml

actions.oldValue: Jordan E. Cooper's comedy at the Belasco, produced by Lee Daniels; opened Dec 1, 2022 and closed Dec 23, 2022. Capitalized for up to $5.5 million.
actions.newValue: Jordan E. Cooper's comedy at the Belasco, produced by Lee Daniels; opened Dec 1, 2022 and closed Dec 23, 2022. Its amended SEC filing (Jan 2023) shows the offering capitalized at $5.7 million.
actions.description: aint-no-mo-2022: notes give the raised amount

actions.newValue: Broadway Journal (Apr 30, 2019): "Tootsie ... is capitalized at $20 million and has a weekly breakeven of $858,000, according to offering documents obtained by Broadway Journal." https://www.broadwayjournal.com/p/a-nerds-guide-to-the-2019-tony-nominations
